windows-search.name: local_windows_search
windows-search.title: Search the Windows index
windows-search.description: Search indexed local files using native Windows Advanced Query Syntax (AQS), for example 'kind:document budget' or 'ext:pdf invoice'. Searches indexed filenames, properties, and content when a content filter is installed. English AQS keywords are supported. Only indexed locations are searched; an empty result does not prove a file does not exist. Returns absolute local paths that local_files_read can read if the Files plugin is enabled. Does not crawl folders or download files.

query.description: Native Windows AQS query, not SQL.

folder.description: Optional absolute local folder path. Restricts matches to this folder and its descendants.

limit.description: Maximum results; defaults to 20, capped at 100.

windows-clipboard.name: local_clipboard_get
windows-clipboard.title: Read clipboard text
windows-clipboard.description: Read the current Windows clipboard as plain text, locally. Returns hasText and text; empty/non-text clipboards return hasText=false. Text is limited to 50,000 characters with truncated=true when shortened. Does not read images, files, clipboard history, or monitor changes. Clipboard contents may be sensitive and returned text enters the normal chat/tool-result flow. Uses the existing execute-then-review flow, not a pre-access permission prompt.

windows-clipboard.name: local_clipboard_set
windows-clipboard.title: Copy text to the clipboard
windows-clipboard.description: Replace the current Windows clipboard contents with plain text (up to 50,000 characters). An empty string copies empty text. Existing clipboard formats/content are replaced; this cannot be undone by this tool. Does not read clipboard history or start monitoring. Requests no cloud/history storage for the copied data. Uses the existing execute-then-review flow, not a pre-access permission prompt.

windows-clipboard.name: local_clipboard_get_image
windows-clipboard.title: Read a clipboard image
windows-clipboard.description: Read the current Windows clipboard bitmap once and return inline PNG with text metadata. An empty/non-bitmap clipboard returns hasImage=false. Maximum input/output image size 20 MiB and decoded size 16 megapixels; unsupported or oversized images fail safely. No files are saved, clipboard history is not read, and no monitoring starts. Sensitive content enters the normal chat/tool-result flow. PNG bytes exist only in the image block and respect Images in Tool Output Filter; metadata respects Text. Uses existing execute-then-review approval, not a pre-access prompt.

windows-clipboard.name: local_clipboard_set_image
windows-clipboard.title: Copy a local image to the clipboard
windows-clipboard.description: Replace all current clipboard content with a bitmap decoded from one existing absolute local PNG/JPEG/BMP/TIFF path. Reads only the first frame, limited to 20 MiB encoded input/output and 16 megapixels. Rejects network/device paths, links, corrupt and oversized images; no downloads, base64 input, temporary files or saved images. Clipboard history/roaming is disabled. Replacement happens before existing result review and cannot be undone by rejecting review. Returned status respects Text in Tool Output Filter.

windows-clipboard.name: local_clipboard_get_files
windows-clipboard.title: Read clipboard file references
windows-clipboard.description: Read up to 100 existing local file references from the current Windows clipboard storage-item format, limited to 50,000 total path characters. Returns paths, count, hasFiles, hasMore and unsupportedCount. Non-file/virtual/folder/network/device/link or unavailable references are omitted without exposing their paths. Does not read file contents, traverse folders, copy/move files, register Files-page shares, inspect clipboard history, or monitor changes. Paths are text metadata covered by Text in Tool Output Filter. Uses existing execute-then-review approval.

windows-clipboard.name: local_clipboard_set_files
windows-clipboard.title: Copy file references to the clipboard
windows-clipboard.description: Replace current clipboard content with copy-only references to 1-100 existing absolute local files, limited to 50,000 total path characters. Validates every reference before replacement; rejects folders, network/device paths and links. Does not read contents, move/delete files, traverse folders, execute files, or register Files-page shares. Another application can later paste the references; this tool does not paste. History/roaming is disabled. Uses existing execute-then-review flow: rejecting review cannot undo replacement. Returned status/count respects Text in Tool Output Filter and does not echo paths.

windows-window-inspector.name: local_windows_get_active_window
windows-window-inspector.title: Get the active window
windows-window-inspector.description: Read metadata for the current foreground Windows window, which may be AIHappey itself. Returns window handle, process ID/name, title, class name and minimized state, or window=null if none is available. Does not switch focus, capture the screen or inspect UI controls. Metadata is live and may change. Uses the existing execute-then-review flow.

windows-window-inspector.name: local_windows_list_windows
windows-window-inspector.title: List open windows
windows-window-inspector.description: List visible, non-cloaked top-level Windows windows, including minimized windows, with handles, process IDs/names, titles and class names. Not an inventory of every running/background process or windows on other desktops. Results are bounded and may change. Use a returned windowHandle and processId with local_windows_inspect_window. No focusing, screen capture or UI actions. Uses the existing execute-then-review flow.

windows-window-inspector.name: local_windows_inspect_window
windows-window-inspector.title: Inspect window controls
windows-window-inspector.description: Read a bounded Windows UI Automation control-view tree for one visible top-level window returned by the window tools. Supply both its windowHandle and processId to detect stale/reused handles. Returns flat nodes with parent IDs, depth, control type, name, automation ID, class, enabled/offscreen status and available plain-text edit values. Password/protected nodes are redacted and not traversed. Never clicks, invokes, types, focuses, expands, captures screens, or elevates. Inaccessible/elevated apps, custom controls and hung providers may yield partial results or a safe error. Depth, nodes, text and waiting time are capped. Sensitive visible text may enter the normal chat/tool-result flow. Uses the existing execute-then-review flow, not a pre-access permission prompt.

windowHandle.description: Opaque hexadecimal windowHandle returned by a window tool; never a JSON number.

windows-window-inspector.name: local_windows_list_screens
windows-window-inspector.title: List screens
windows-window-inspector.description: List up to 32 currently attached Windows screens with screenId, desktop bounds in pixels, and primary status. Use a returned screenId for direct screen capture with local_windows_capture. Screen identities and layout can change; no screenshot is taken by listing.

windows-window-inspector.name: local_windows_capture
windows-window-inspector.title: Capture a window or screen
windows-window-inspector.description: Capture one frame locally using Windows Graphics Capture. For source=window supply windowHandle and processId from the existing window tools; for source=screen supply screenId from local_windows_list_screens. Omit source or use picker to let the user select a window/screen in the native Windows picker. If a valid direct target cannot be captured, the native picker is offered as fallback; malformed or stale window identities fail safely. Canceling the picker returns canceled=true. Returns inline PNG plus text metadata, never saves a file or retains a capture session. Limited to 16 megapixels and 20 MiB encoded PNG. Does not focus, restore, or automate the target. Protected/minimized/closed windows may be unavailable or blank. Sensitive visible content enters the normal tool-result/chat flow; outgoing image and text blocks respect Tool Output Filter settings. Uses existing execute-then-review approval, not a new pre-capture approval prompt. Native picker selection is separate from result review.

source.description: Selects the capture mode. Omit or use picker for native user selection; all target selectors are ignored in picker mode. Only selectors for the selected source are used.

windowHandle.description: Required only for source=window, together with processId. Use a handle returned by the existing window tools. Ignored for screen/picker.

processId.description: Required only for source=window; must match the selected window's process. Ignored for screen/picker.

screenId.description: Required only for source=screen; use an identity returned by local_windows_list_screens. Ignored for window/picker.

windows-window-inspector.name: local_windows_activate_window
windows-window-inspector.title: Activate a window
windows-window-inspector.description: Request foreground activation of one visible top-level local window using Win32. Supply its exact windowHandle and processId from the window tools; stale identities fail. Does not restore minimized windows: use restore separately if needed. Windows may refuse foreground activation; submitted/completed and observed foreground/minimized/bounds report the actual outcome. No clicks, keystrokes, input-thread attachment, elevation, or foreground-lock bypass. Uses existing execute-once-then-review flow; rejected review cannot undo focus changes. Status respects Text in Tool Output Filter.

windows-window-inspector.name: local_windows_minimize_window
windows-window-inspector.title: Minimize a window
windows-window-inspector.description: Request Win32 minimization of one visible top-level window identified by windowHandle and processId. Revalidates identity immediately before acting. Does not close the window, automate controls, send input or elevate. The asynchronous native request is observed for up to one second; submitted=true with completed=false means queued/unconfirmed, not guaranteed success. Returns current foreground/minimized/bounds. Uses existing execute-once-then-review flow; rejecting review cannot undo minimization and does not repeat it. Status respects Text in Tool Output Filter.

windows-window-inspector.name: local_windows_restore_window
windows-window-inspector.title: Restore a window
windows-window-inspector.description: Request Win32 restoration of a minimized/maximized visible top-level window using its windowHandle and processId. Restoration may activate the target; no foreground-lock bypass is attempted. Stale identities fail safely. Returns submitted/completed and observed foreground/minimized/bounds after up to one second; a queued request is not guaranteed success. No input simulation, control automation or elevation. Executes once before existing result review; rejecting review cannot undo restoration. Status respects Text in Tool Output Filter.

windows-window-inspector.name: local_windows_reposition_window
windows-window-inspector.title: Move or resize a window
windows-window-inspector.description: Request Win32 positioning of one visible top-level window identified by windowHandle and processId. x/y are signed virtual-desktop pixel coordinates, including negative coordinates on secondary screens. Supply both width and height to resize (1-32768 pixels each), or omit both to preserve size. Coordinate sums must fit signed 32-bit integers. Does not activate, restore, change z-order, click, type or elevate. Minimized/maximized apps may ignore or constrain positioning. Returns observed bounds and submitted/completed after up to one second; accepted/queued is not guaranteed completion. Executes once before existing result review; rejection cannot undo changes. Status respects Text in Tool Output Filter.

windows-notifications.name: local_notifications_show
windows-notifications.title: Show a Windows notification
windows-notifications.description: Submit one immediate native Windows app notification with plain-text title and body through AppNotificationManager. No buttons, click commands, custom activation, scheduling, history management, downloads or network access. Returns submitted=true and the native notification ID, not a guarantee it was displayed/read: Windows notification settings or Do Not Disturb may suppress presentation. Unsupported, disabled or unregistered hosts fail safely without fallback infrastructure. No app-side notification state is stored. Submission happens once before existing result review; rejecting review cannot retract it. Returned status respects Text in Tool Output Filter and does not echo the title/body.

windows-ocr.name: local_ocr_list_languages
windows-ocr.title: List local OCR languages
windows-ocr.description: List installed Windows OCR recognition languages and the maximum supported image dimension. Runs locally and installs/downloads nothing. An empty list means the user needs to install a Windows OCR language pack through Windows Settings.

windows-ocr.name: local_ocr_recognize_text
windows-ocr.title: Recognize text in a local image
windows-ocr.description: Extract text from a local PNG, JPEG, BMP or TIFF image with installed Windows OCR, without any model/API/network request. Supply an absolute local path, optionally an installed BCP-47 language tag from local_ocr_list_languages; otherwise Windows user languages are used. Reads only the first image frame. Rejects network/device paths, links, oversized files and images above 16 megapixels or the native OCR dimension limit; does not resize. Returns text and bounded lines/word rectangles in decoded-image pixels, with truncation indicators. Maximum file size 20 MiB, text 50,000 characters, lines 500, words 2,000. No screen capture, PDF processing, language downloads, or external OCR fallback. Extracted text enters the normal chat/tool-result flow.

path.description: Absolute local image path; for example C:\Users\Alice\Pictures\error.png.

language.description: Optional installed Windows OCR language tag, such as en-US or nl-NL.

windows-system-information.name: local_system_get_info
windows-system-information.title: Read system information
windows-system-information.description: Read a local .NET/Win32 snapshot of CPU model, architecture and logical processor count, total/available/used physical memory in bytes, memory load percentage, and Windows version/build. Does not sample CPU utilization, collect device identifiers, query remote services, run commands, or retain monitoring state. Returned text follows the normal tool-result flow and Text Output Filter setting. Uses existing execute-then-review approval.

windows-system-information.name: local_system_list_processes
windows-system-information.title: List running processes
windows-system-information.description: Read a bounded local snapshot of running process IDs, names, working-set bytes and cumulative CPU time in milliseconds (not utilization). Optional case-insensitive name substring query. Default 50 results, maximum 200, ordered by process ID. Inaccessible/exited processes may be skipped or have null metrics; partial and hasMore indicate incomplete results. No command lines, environment variables, executable paths, process control, elevation, monitoring, or remote access. Returned text respects the Text Output Filter. Uses existing execute-then-review approval.

windows-app-launcher.name: local_apps_list
windows-app-launcher.title: List installed applications
windows-app-launcher.description: Discover installed applications from the local Windows Apps folder, returning appId and name. Optional case-insensitive name/ID substring query; default 50 results, capped at 100, with hasMore. Search with a more specific query when truncated. No filesystem crawling, downloads, launching, or retained catalog. Some listed entries cannot be launched because their shortcuts contain arguments or require elevation. Returned text respects the Text Output Filter.

windows-app-launcher.name: local_apps_launch
windows-app-launcher.title: Open an app, document, or URL
windows-app-launcher.description: Use native ShellExecute(open) for a single target: kind=app with an exact installed appId from local_apps_list; kind=executable with an existing absolute local .exe path; kind=document with an existing supported local document path; or kind=url with an HTTP/HTTPS URL. No arguments, arbitrary command strings, scripts, shortcuts, custom URI schemes, runas, or elevation. Local paths reject network/device paths and links. Supported documents: txt/md/log/json/xml/yaml/yml/csv/tsv/pdf/rtf/docx/xlsx/pptx/odt/ods/odp, PNG/JPEG/BMP/GIF/TIFF/WebP, MP3/WAV/FLAC/MP4/MKV/WebM. Executables/handlers must be native Windows executables with an explicit asInvoker manifest, not auto-elevating; legacy/unverifiable targets fail safely. Installed shortcut entries with arguments are rejected. No application output is captured; success means Windows accepted the open request, not that the app finished or the document loaded. Opening a URL may cause the user's browser to access the network; these tools do not fetch it. Launches occur before existing result review, so rejecting review cannot undo a launch. Returned text respects the Text Output Filter and review/continuation never relaunches the target.

local-files.name: local_files_list
local-files.title: List shared files and folders
local-files.description: List references explicitly shared through the Windows Files page, including AI-created files. References contain stable IDs, paths, kind, and availability; the app does not copy file contents. Use IDs with the shared directory/read/create tools. Names may not be unique. Sharing a folder includes its descendants and permits creation of new files there. This list does not restrict the separate local_files_read absolute-path reader. Use nextCursor to continue; roots may change between calls.

cursor.description: Omit or use an empty string for the first page. For continuation, pass nextCursor returned by the previous shared-item listing unchanged.

local-files.name: local_files_list_directory
local-files.title: Browse a shared folder
local-files.description: List direct children of a shared folder or any nested subfolder. Pass the folder reference ID and a root-relative relativePath (omit for the root). Returned relativePath values are always relative to that shared root; use them to browse deeper or read files. No recursion or whole-disk scanning is performed. Returns files, folders, and explicit unsupported/denied/unavailable entries; links/junctions are never traversed. Pages are bounded; continue with nextCursor, the same ID and relativePath. Cursors are opaque, single-use, and valid only for this chat turn; restart the listing if expired. Directory contents can change between pages.

id.description: Shared folder ID returned by local_files_list.

relativePath.description: Subfolder path relative to the shared root; omitted or empty for the root. No absolute paths or dot/dot-dot segments.

cursor.description: Omit or use an empty string for the first page. For continuation, pass the single-use nextCursor returned by the previous directory page unchanged.

local-files.name: local_files_read_shared
local-files.title: Read a shared file
local-files.description: Read extracted text from an explicitly shared file ID, or from a file within a shared folder ID using a root-relative relativePath. Uses the same PDF/plain-text extractor as local_files_read; does not support OCR, Office formats, network paths or links. Paging is 1-based extracted-text lines, not PDF pages. Use nextLine as startLine to continue. Files can change between reads. A removed reference cannot be used, although another overlapping share may still allow access.

id.description: Shared file or folder reference ID.

relativePath.description: Required for a file inside a shared folder; omitted for a directly shared file.

local-files.name: local_files_create
local-files.title: Create a file in a shared folder
local-files.description: Create a NEW file inside an explicitly shared folder or existing nested subfolder. Requires the shared folder ID and a root-relative destination relativePath. Existing files/directories are never overwritten, renamed or deleted; missing parent folders are not created. No absolute paths, traversal, network paths or links. data is UTF-8 text by default; use encoding=base64 for explicitly encoded binary bytes. Maximum decoded file size is 1 MiB. Merely giving text a PDF/Office extension does not generate that format. The file is written to the real shared folder and registered as a reference on the Files page, not copied into app storage or executed. Sharing a folder authorizes creation; the existing execute-then-review flow is retained. A successful creation can include a warning if reference registration/refresh fails; do not retry creation of that same destination.

relativePath.description: New filename including any existing subfolders, relative to the shared root.

data.description: UTF-8 text or base64-encoded bytes, matching encoding.

local-files.name: local_files_read
local-files.title: Read a local file
local-files.description: Read text from an absolute local file path, including paths returned by local_windows_search. Uses the shared document extractor for PDFs and recognized text/Markdown/JSON/YAML/XML/source files. Does not support OCR, Office documents, downloads, network paths, device paths, or symbolic links. Paging uses 1-based line numbers in extracted text (not PDF page numbers). Results include totalLines, startLine, endLine, truncated, and nextLine; request nextLine as startLine to continue. A text-size ceiling can shorten a page at a complete line boundary. Files may change between calls.

path.description: Absolute local filesystem path, for example C:\Users\Alice\Documents\report.pdf.

maxLines.description: Maximum lines to return; defaults to 200, capped at 2000.
